evidence: Dimension level: task tests/scoring.toml is byte-equal to the template: [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. score.py (byte-equal to template, lines 40-48) zeroes reward unless both gates pass and functional > 0.05, so gates carry no mass and real functionality carries 60%. Pure style (visual likert) is capped at 0.2; polish (0.2) is not style here: all five polish rows are binary browser-observed behaviours (input/focus/scroll preservation under live updates, failed-send recovery, session-expiry resume). Visual prompt line 12 says likert raw 1 normalizes to zero, so a broken/static shell earns no style mass. Criterion level (computed with tomllib): functional 43 binary criteria, sum 58.5. Heaviest (2.5 = 0.0256 reward each): hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private - exactly the brief's stated 'hard part' (instruction.md:1 'nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts') and its explicit 'must never see' privacy promise (instruction.md:9). 2.0 tier: bulk all-or-none, undo restore/conflict, refused-put-back (public at hireops_rules.md:85), thread paging, unread counts/scrolled-up, drafts (instruction.md:7). Lightest (0.5): hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate (their success path is already proven by the hro_gate_shared gate), hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked - narrow edge legs. Polish sum 12: pol_live_board 3, pol_live_thread 3, session_resume 2.5, earlier_place 2, failed_send 1.5 - again weighted toward the brief's emphasized 'leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone' (instruction.md:7). Visual: five likert rows, equal 1.2 each (sum 6), with described 5-level anchors. No weight in any [judge] block; all weights positive. Max non-functional contribution sanity check: 0.4 total, of which only 0.2 is style. Weak-app attempt: an app passing both gates plus just enough functional rows to clear the floor (>2.925 of 58.5, e.g. job_open+add_candidate+add_email_rules+move_one_stage = 3.5 -> 0.036 reward) with flawless visuals (0.2) and the two polish rows that need no live channel (session_resume+failed_send = 4/12 -> 0.067) tops out near 0.30; a functionally complete app with mediocre visuals (likert 3s) and full polish scores ~0.9. No weight arrangement lets style outrank function. Conforming-alternative attempt: an app delivering live updates by polling rather than websockets, or storing drafts server-side, is not penalized by any weight; nothing weights an unrequired detail heavily. Notes (not defects): (1) because functional is spread over 43 rows, each single visual likert row (0.04) is worth more than the single heaviest functional row (0.0256); this is a consequence of the template-fixed 0.6/0.2/0.2 shares that row reviewers may not alter, and aggregate functionality still outweighs style 3:1. (2) Half of polish (pol_live_board/pol_live_thread, 0.10 reward) is 0 if no live update arrives, on top of functional hro_live_board/hro_msg_exchange; this stacks the live-sync penalty but matches the brief's central concurrency theme and correctly ranks 'no live updates' below 'live updates that clobber input'. (3) hro_activity (whole audit log incl. filter) carries weight 1, modest for its breadth but not dishonest.
